brief: A MIXED forest seen from the side, simple and clear for a child: exactly two kinds of trees mixed together in one row — round leafy deciduous trees (maple, birch with white bark) standing right next to pointed dark-green conifers (fir, spruce) with needles. Alternate them: leafy, pointed, leafy, pointed, leafy. Both kinds clearly visible and easy to tell apart. Light background, grass at the bottom. No people, no text.
One single large green MAPLE LEAF, flat, with its five pointed lobes and its stem, centered on a light plain background, like a nature sticker. Clearly a broad leaf, not needles. No text.

One single SPRUCE BRANCH covered in short sharp green NEEDLES, with one small brown pine cone (cocotte) hanging from it, centered on a light plain background, like a nature sticker. Clearly needles, not flat leaves. No text.

A birchbark canoe around the year 1500: two original Iroquoian people paddling a canoe made of light birch BARK sewn on a wooden frame, on a calm river bordered by a forest of maples and birches. The bark texture of the canoe is clearly visible. Respectful and dignified. No text.
